case_title: Mukesh & Anr. v. State for NCT of Delhi & Ors.
accused_occupation: Bus helper/cleaner (Akshay); bus driver (Mukesh, per the judgment's account of the bus crew)
accused_socioeconomic_status: Poor/ordinary background (stated by the accused in their affidavits; not a court finding)
previous_criminal_record: Not stated (accused claimed no criminal antecedents in affidavits; court made no finding)
accused_victim_relationship: Stranger (no prior connection between the accused and the victim is described)
weapon: Iron rods (two), inserted into the victim's private parts; bodily assault with hands and kicks
evidence_type: Dying declarations (three); eyewitness testimony of the victim's friend; medical evidence; DNA and fingerprint analysis; odontology (bite mark) report; CCTV footage; recovery of articles on disclosure statements; test identification parade
confession: None relied on; disclosure statements were used only for recoveries under s.27 Evidence Act
aggravating_circumstances: Gang rape in a moving bus; anal and oral sex forced; iron rods inserted into private parts causing intestinal perforation and sepsis; bite marks (10); victims robbed; victims thrown from bus in cold winter night; attempt to run them over; destruction of evidence
mitigating_circumstances: Poverty and rural background; aged parents and young children; conduct in custody; claimed reformation; young age (as argued); no criminal antecedents (claimed)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of all charges; death sentence under s.302 IPC; life imprisonment for s.120B and s.376(2)(g); terms of years for other offences; sentences ordered to run concurrently
high_court_outcome: Conviction affirmed; death penalty confirmed for all four
offence_finally_established: Criminal conspiracy (s.120B); murder (s.302 r/w s.120B); gang rape (s.376(2)(g) r/w Explanation 1, per Banumathi J.) and other convicted offences upheld as trial court found
neutral_facts: On the night of 16 December 2012 the victim and a male friend boarded a chartered white bus at a bus stand in South Delhi. Six occupants were inside. After the bus moved, its lights were switched off. The friend was held down and beaten with iron rods, while the victim was taken to the rear of the bus and raped repeatedly by several men in turn, including anal and oral sex. Iron rods were inserted into her vagina and rectum. Her belongings and the friend's were robbed. Both were then thrown from the moving bus, and the bus was turned to run over them. The victim suffered severe internal injuries and died of sepsis with multiple organ failure in Singapore on 29 December 2012. Investigators recovered the bus, CCTV footage of the bus near the dumping spot, and blood-stained iron rods. DNA profiles from blood on the rods and on clothing matched the victim and the friend. A bite-mark comparison linked two accused to bite marks on the victim. Articles belonging to the victim and friend were recovered on the accused's disclosure statements. The victim gave several statements in hospital, including a later one written in gestures and writing, naming the accused.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from sepsis and multi-organ failure after multiple internal injuries (intestinal perforation, rectal and vaginal tears, bite marks); friend suffered head and body injuries
number_of_offences: 12 charged (IPC ss.120B, 365, 366, 307, 376(2)(g), 377, 396, 302, 395, 397, 201, 412); 11 finally upheld (s.396 was charged but not convicted)
financial_property_loss: Cash of Rs.1,000, mobile phones, debit and credit cards, watches, rings, shoes, clothing and a purse taken from the friend and the victim
premeditation_planning: Court found a concert/agreement formed once the victim and friend boarded; no separate premeditation finding beyond this
motive: Sexual gratification and sadistic pleasure (as found by the court from the conduct)
key_evidence_accepted: Three consistent dying declarations (including one by gestures and writing); eyewitness PW-1 testimony; medical and OT records; DNA reports linking accused and blood on rods to victim; odontology report linking two accused; CCTV footage and bus identification; fingerprint report placing one accused in the bus; recovery of victim and friend's articles
witness_credibility: Friend-eyewitness found credible; injuries lent assurance of presence; omissions in FIR held not fatal; injured-witness testimony given greater weight
post_offence_conduct: Attempted to run over the victims; washed the bus; burnt clothing; divided the loot; one accused fled when police approached the bus (Ram Singh); accused led police to recoveries
custody_duration: Approximately four years (per the court's reference to custody by early 2017)
trial_duration: offence: 16 December 2012 (night of 16/17 Dec 2012); trial judgment: 10.09.2013; High Court: 13.03.2014; Supreme Court: not given
legal_representation: Accused: M.L. Sharma and A.P. Singh (with associates); amici curiae Raju Ramachandran and Sanjay R. Hegde. State: Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Adv.
investigation_status: FIR registered 17.12.2012; investigation completed; chargesheet filed 03.01.2013; supplementary chargesheet 04.02.2013; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Amicus argued s.235(2) CrPC was not effectively complied with on sentence; court itself gave the accused opportunity by affidavits. Overwriting of date on a forwarding note was found insignificant
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, death sentence. High Court: conviction affirmed, death confirmed. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Crime falls in rarest of rare category; devastation of social trust warrants death penalty; conviction on conspiracy and gang rape based on dying declarations, scientific and recovery evidence
defence_argument: Investigation flawed and biased; FIR delayed and crafted; PW-1 unreliable and improved his version; dying declarations tutored; DNA and bus evidence planted; plea of alibi; mitigating circumstances warranting commutation
legal_principle_applied: Conspiracy inferred from circumstances; gang rape joint liability (s.376(2)(g) Explanation 1); dying declaration reliability; DNA reports accepted unless absolutely dented; s.27 recoveries; rarest of rare doctrine; s.235(2) hearing
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684; Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab (1983) 3 SCC 470; Pulukuri Kottaya v. Emperor AIR 1947 PC 67; Laxman v. State of Maharashtra (2002) 6 SCC 710; Atbir v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi (2010) 9 SCC 1; Dagdu v. State of Maharashtra (1977) 3 SCC 68; Ram Jag v. State of U.P. (1974) 4 SCC 201
sentencing_rationale: Gruesome gang rape, insertion of iron rods, and callous abandonment of victims in cold night shock the collective conscience; aggravating circumstances outweigh mitigating ones; life imprisonment held inadequate
judicial_mitigating_factors: Considered (family circumstances, young age, conduct in jail, reformation prospects) but held outweighed by aggravating factors
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutality and diabolic manner of the crime; sadistic conduct; use of iron rods; bite marks; disposal of victims in cold night; attempt to kill by running them over; destruction of evidence; shock to collective conscience
other_sentence_order: Trial court recommended compensation under s.357A CrPC to victim's heirs; Supreme Court permitted accused affidavits on sentence and gave gender-justice recommendations (Banumathi J.)
